questions.question: @media (max-width: 600px) applies when the viewport is:
questions.explanation: max-width is inclusive of the value: styles apply at 600px and below (mobile-first uses min-width instead).

questions.question: Mobile-first CSS typically uses:

options.text: min-width queries (base styles for small, enhance upward)

questions.explanation: Mobile-first: write base for small screens, then min-width breakpoints add layouts for larger devices.

questions.question: The 'only screen' prefix is used to:

options.text: Hide the query from very old browsers that don't support media queries

questions.explanation: only prevents legacy browsers from applying the styles; mostly historical now but still harmless.

questions.question: Media features can be combined with:
questions.explanation: Use 'and' to require multiple features, commas for OR (independent queries), and 'not' to negate.

questions.question: prefers-color-scheme: dark targets users who:

options.text: Have their OS set to dark mode

questions.explanation: prefers-color-scheme (dark/light) reads the OS theme — pairs with CSS variables for automatic dark mode.

questions.question: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce signals the user wants:
questions.explanation: Respect it by disabling/reducing non-essential motion — critical for users sensitive to movement.

questions.question: An orientation: portrait query matches when:

options.text: The viewport height is greater than or equal to its width

questions.explanation: portrait = taller than wide; landscape = wider than tall. Commonly used for layout swaps on phones.

questions.question: Breakpoints should ideally be based on:

options.text: Your content/layout needs, not specific device widths

questions.explanation: Design for content breakpoints (where the layout breaks), not a fixed list of devices — more future-proof.
